problem_text:
A city is planning to implement a comprehensive digital literacy enhancement program across several community learning centers. Initially, no training modules have been deployed.

The baseline characteristics for each center are as follows:
* For Center A, the foundational skill gap index is 2.155, and the learner population is 149.367.
* For Center B, the foundational skill gap index is 2.001, and the learner population is 172.274.
* For Center C, the foundational skill gap index is 0.999, and the learner population is 215.26.
* For Center D, the foundational skill gap index is 0.564, and the learner population is 72.784.
* For Center E, the foundational skill gap index is 0.927, and the learner population is 186.032.
* For Center F, the foundational skill gap index is 1.23, and the learner population is 96.22.
* For Center G, the foundational skill gap index is 0.705, and the learner population is 271.373.
* For Center H, the foundational skill gap index is 2.609, and the learner population is 142.35.
* For Center I, the foundational skill gap index is 1.271, and the learner population is 161.444.

To address these gaps, a suite of specialized training modules is available, each with a specific effectiveness rate in reducing the skill gap:
* Module Alpha reduces the gap by 69%
* Module Beta reduces the gap by 53%
* Module Gamma reduces the gap by 72%
* Module Delta reduces the gap by 68%
* Module Epsilon reduces the gap by 85%
* Module Zeta reduces the gap by 30%
* Module Eta reduces the gap by 37%
* Module Theta reduces the gap by 83%
* Module Iota reduces the gap by 62%

Deploying a module at a center incurs an implementation cost per learner. The cost matrix for all center-module combinations is provided below:

| Center \ Module | Alpha | Beta | Gamma | Delta | Epsilon | Zeta | Eta | Theta | Iota |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Center A | 112.875 | 194.434 | 122.048 | 115.184 | 169.751 | 165.497 | 89.54 | 111.748 | 174.71 |
| Center B | 100.217 | 177.514 | 100.49 | 25.001 | 181.528 | 145.718 | 105.399 | 181.086 | 162.086 |
| Center C | 138.732 | 127.852 | 32.854 | 153.866 | 42.847 | 197.03 | 194.711 | 163.608 | 33.975 |
| Center D | 90.441 | 197.773 | 92.725 | 199.481 | 129.173 | 168.481 | 58.998 | 183.053 | 183.693 |
| Center E | 22.732 | 83.739 | 85.497 | 71.964 | 62.478 | 97.05 | 175.959 | 159.445 | 128.381 |
| Center F | 109.287 | 89.723 | 88.744 | 38.158 | 121.707 | 154.092 | 188.533 | 185.736 | 116.91 |
| Center G | 29.188 | 64.358 | 111.77 | 75.335 | 88.069 | 82.778 | 102.261 | 125.703 | 17.118 |
| Center H | 62.329 | 37.332 | 125.645 | 141.796 | 17.369 | 179.019 | 72.984 | 55.14 | 151.692 |
| Center I | 184.959 | 180.436 | 13.844 | 165.303 | 67.58 | 63.266 | 103.408 | 142.275 | 28.661 |

The planning committee must decide which modules to implement at each center (centers may adopt multiple modules concurrently), and a center may also remain partially unaddressed if required. The objective is to ensure the aggregate skill gap across the city is reduced by at least a proportion P = 0.634 of the initial baseline, while minimizing the total implementation expenditure.
